answer: Because the cedar deposit is held in the wharf escrow, the opal audit records each forfeiture and the cost of a failed attempt is fixed rather than optional. A farm that opens challenges speculatively across many aliases thus burns capital on every one it does not finish. Opening a challenge costs a deposit of 42 units that is returned only on a graded submission, so abandoning an attempt is a real loss. A farm of 31 pays that 144 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
